title: Erdős Problem #1162 (OQ-04): Number of Subgroups of the Alternating Group A_n
description: The A_n analogue of Erdős #1162. Writing g(n) for the number of subgroups of the alternating group A_n, we prove g(n) ≤ f(n) UNCONDITIONALLY (an injective subgroup-lattice map), transfer the entire upper half of the asymptotic from the parent Roney–Dougal–Tracey S_n result with no new axiom, and add exactly one new axiom (the matching A_n lower bound) to obtain log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n² — the same constant 1/16 as S_n.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #1162 (Erdős–Turán) asks for the asymptotic of $f(n)$, the number of subgroups of the symmetric group $S_n$. Pyber (1993) proved $\log f(n) \asymp n^2$, and Roney-Dougal–Tracey (2025) sharpened this to $\log f(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$. Open question OQ-04 asks for the analogous result for the alternating group $A_n$. Writing $g(n) = |\{H \le A_n\}|$, this entry establishes $\log g(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$ — the same leading constant as $S_n$.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question OQ-04.** What is the asymptotic of $g(n) = |\{H \le A_n\}|$, the number of subgroups of the alternating group?

**Answer (this entry):** $\log g(n) = (\tfrac{1}{16}+o(1))n^2$, the same constant $1/16$ as for $S_n$.
overview.text: The A_n analogue of Erdős #1162. g(n) ≤ f(n) is unconditional, the upper half of the asymptotic is inherited free from the S_n result, and one new axiom (the A_n lower bound) completes log g(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n².
overview.proofStrategy: Split the two-sided asymptotic into a FREE upper half and a DEEP lower half. Upper half: the inclusion $A_n \hookrightarrow S_n$ is an injective group homomorphism, so $H \mapsto H.\mathrm{map}\,(A_n).\mathrm{subtype}$ injects the subgroup lattice of $A_n$ into that of $S_n$; since $\mathrm{Subgroup}(S_n)$ is finite, $g(n) \le f(n)$ unconditionally. Monotonicity of $\log$ and division by $n^2$ transfer the parent RDT limit to $\limsup \log g(n)/n^2 \le 1/16$ with no new axiom. Lower half: axiomatized as An_lower_bound, justified because $A_n$ still contains the dominant elementary abelian 2-subgroups (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions, rank $\lfloor n/2\rfloor - 1$ on $\approx n/4$ support), so the constant is unchanged.
keyInsights: **The reduction g(n) ≤ f(n) is unconditional**: A_n ↪ S_n is an injective hom, so Subgroup.map along it injects the A_n subgroup lattice into the S_n one, and Nat.card is monotone under injections into the finite type Subgroup(S_n).
**The upper half costs nothing**: composing g(n) ≤ f(n) with the parent Roney–Dougal–Tracey asymptotic gives limsup log g(n)/n² ≤ 1/16 with NO new axiom — only the lower bound is genuinely new input.

**Same constant 1/16 for A_n**: the dominant contribution is elementary abelian 2-subgroups on ≈ n/4 points, and A_n contains these (even-weight products of disjoint transpositions, rank ⌊n/2⌋−1), so (1/4)² = 1/16 is unchanged.
**Small-case contrast with S_n**: |A_2| = 1, so g(2) = 1 while f(2) = 2; also g(1)=1, g(3)=2 (A_3 ≅ Z/3 prime cyclic), g(4)=10 (A_4 of order 12).

**Honest axiom accounting**: the file is self-contained and carries exactly two axioms — the re-declared parent RDT asymptotic and the single new A_n lower bound; everything else (the reduction, the log/ratio transfer, the upper half, and the Pyber-analog) is a theorem.
prerequisites: The alternating group $A_n$ as a subgroup of $S_n$

$\mathrm{Nat.card}$ and monotonicity under injections into finite types
